papers.title: Retrospective Case-Control Study Genes Related to Bone Metabolism That Justify the Condition of Periodontal Disease and Failure of Dental Implants in Patients with down Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Down syndrome patients show success rates in dental implants much lower than those observed in the general population. This retrospective case-control study aimed to identify possible genes that are related to the regulation of inflammatory responses and bone metabolism related to periimplantitis and implant loss, as well as genes related to bone quality. This process involved using the functional analysis of the gene expression software Transcriptome Analysis Console (TAC version 4.0 Applied BiosystemsTM, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) and a search for possible candidate genes involved. The focus was placed on the 93 genes related to periodontitis, periimplantitis, bone loss, implant loss, and genes related to bone quality and regulators underlying the establishment and maintenance of osseointegration. Five genes showed statistically significant results (p < 0.05) in our comparison. Four of them, IL1B (p = 0.023), IL1RN (p = 0.048), BGLAP (p = 0.0372) and PTK2 (p = 0.0075) were down-regulated in the periodontal disease and implant rejection group, and only one was overexpressed: FOXO1A (p = 0.0552). The genes with statistically significant alterations described in this article determine that the group of Down syndrome patients with periodontal disease and implant failure is a group of patients genetically susceptible to suffering from both conditions together.

papers.title: You Never Get a Second Chance To Make a Good First Impression: Seeding Active Learning for 3D Semantic Segmentation
papers.abstract: We propose SeedAL, a method to seed active learning for efficient annotation of 3D point clouds for semantic segmentation. Active Learning (AL) iteratively selects relevant data fractions to annotate within a given budget, but requires a first fraction of the dataset (a 'seed') to be already annotated to estimate the benefit of annotating other data fractions. We first show that the choice of the seed can significantly affect the performance of many AL methods. We then propose a method for automatically constructing a seed that will ensure good performance for AL. Assuming that images of the point clouds are available, which is common, our method relies on powerful unsupervised image features to measure the diversity of the point clouds. It selects the point clouds for the seed by optimizing the diversity under an annotation budget, which can be done by solving a linear optimization problem. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach compared to random seeding and existing methods on both the S3DIS and SemanticKitti datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/nerminsamet/seedal.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注3D点云语义分割的主动学习种子选择，与FEA代理建模或生物力学设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on active learning for 3D semantic segmentation of point clouds, with no application to finite element analysis, surrogate modeling, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanical implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 主动学习需要初始标注种子，种子选择影响后续性能。
summary_zh.method: 利用无监督图像特征优化多样性，通过线性规划选择种子点云。
summary_zh.result: 所提方法在S3DIS和SemanticKitti数据集上优于随机种子和现有方法。
summary_zh.validation: 在标准3D语义分割基准上验证。

summary_en.motivation: The initial seed selection significantly impacts the performance of active learning for 3D semantic segmentation, yet existing methods rely on random seeding.
summary_en.method: SeedAL leverages unsupervised image features to measure point cloud diversity and selects an optimal seed set by solving a linear optimization problem under annotation budget constraints.
summary_en.result: The proposed method outperforms random seeding and existing active learning approaches on the S3DIS and SemanticKitti datasets.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on standard 3D semantic segmentation benchmarks with numerical comparisons.

papers.title: Quantile Extreme Gradient Boosting for Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: As the availability, size and complexity of data have increased in recent years, machine learning (ML) techniques have become popular for modeling. Predictions resulting from applying ML models are often used for inference, decision-making, and downstream applications. A crucial yet often overlooked aspect of ML is uncertainty quantification, which can significantly impact how predictions from models are used and interpreted.   Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) is one of the most popular ML methods given its simple implementation, fast computation, and sequential learning, which make its predictions highly accurate compared to other methods. However, techniques for uncertainty determination in ML models such as XGBoost have not yet been universally agreed among its varying applications. We propose enhancements to XGBoost whereby a modified quantile regression is used as the objective function to estimate uncertainty (QXGBoost). Specifically, we included the Huber norm in the quantile regression model to construct a differentiable approximation to the quantile regression error function. This key step allows XGBoost, which uses a gradient-based optimization algorithm, to make probabilistic predictions efficiently.   QXGBoost was applied to create 90\% prediction intervals for one simulated dataset and one real-world environmental dataset of measured traffic noise. Our proposed method had comparable or better performance than the uncertainty estimates generated for regular and quantile light gradient boosting. For both the simulated and traffic noise datasets, the overall performance of the prediction intervals from QXGBoost were better than other models based on coverage width-based criterion.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出的分位数梯度提升方法可用于代理模型的不确定性量化，可迁移至植入物设计的FEA代理建模。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA surrogate application, no biomechanics or implant design context, no constraint handling or multi-objective optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 机器学习模型缺乏不确定性量化，影响决策可靠性。
summary_zh.method: 在XGBoost中引入Huber范数近似分位数回归损失函数，实现概率预测。
summary_zh.result: QXGBoost在模拟和交通噪声数据集上生成90%预测区间，性能优于对比方法。
summary_zh.validation: 在模拟数据集和真实交通噪声数据集上验证预测区间覆盖率和宽度。

summary_en.motivation: Machine learning models often lack uncertainty quantification, which is critical for reliable decision-making.
summary_en.method: A modified quantile regression with Huber norm is integrated into XGBoost's gradient-based optimization to enable probabilistic predictions.
summary_en.result: QXGBoost produces 90% prediction intervals with comparable or better coverage width-based criterion than quantile light gradient boosting on simulated and real-world traffic noise data.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on one simulated dataset and one real-world environmental dataset using prediction interval coverage and width metrics.

papers.title: Stochastic Cell Transmission Models of Traffic Networks
papers.abstract: We introduce a rigorous framework for stochastic cell transmission models for general traffic networks. The performance of traffic systems is evaluated based on preference functionals and acceptable designs. The numerical implementation combines simulation, Gaussian process regression, and a stochastic exploration procedure. The approach is illustrated in two case studies.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究交通网络的随机元胞传输模型，与生物力学有限元代理建模无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses traffic flow modeling, not biomedical FEA surrogate modeling; it lacks implant mechanics, biomechanical constraints, and experimental validation.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高交通网络性能评估的采样效率。
summary_zh.method: 结合仿真、高斯过程回归和随机探索的框架。
summary_zh.result: 通过两个案例验证了方法的有效性。

summary_en.motivation: To improve sampling efficiency in performance evaluation of traffic networks under uncertainty.
summary_en.method: A framework combining simulation, Gaussian process regression, and stochastic exploration for stochastic cell transmission models.
summary_en.result: The approach is demonstrated on two case studies, showing effective surrogate-based optimization.
summary_en.validation: Validation via numerical simulation case studies.
